messages:
lucas: quick thought  manifest-driven release + small bot flags to reduce manual release-note churn and make rollbacks trivial.

priya: ok show the minimal flow.

lucas: author YAML manifest, run rlsctl publish -> signs & uploads, then release-bot apply --manifest-url=... --approve. dry-run supported.

emma: can manifest include changelog template so we don't paste the same bullets?

lucas: yes. sample keys: services, rollout, safety (change_window/lock_until), approvers, changelog.mode (auto/manual).

priya: like `lock_until` to block accidental late pushes? useful.

emma: for rollback UX: release-bot revert --service=web-frontend --to=3.1.9 or revert --manifest-url=...

lucas: bot stores last N pins per service (N=12 default) so `--to=previous` works. also attach audit_id on publish.

ops-bot: permissions note: require at least one approver + check release-team ACL before apply. will enforce.

release-bot: I'll implement flags: --manifest-url, --signature, --dry-run, --hold-until, --annotate. Bot will post generated short release note and pin manifest link.

priya: auto-changelog expansion should list services and approvers, include audit id. also attach perf snapshot if notes_sources present.

emma: emergency option: --expedite --skip-lock limited to release-admin role.

lucas: summary UX: after apply print `Pinned 2 services  strategy rolling  lock_until 2026-04-02T01:55Z  approvals 2` + permalink.

priya: test plan: 1) publish+dry-run, 2) publish+apply in staging, 3) simulate abort condition, 4) revert. I'll open checklist PR.

release-bot: PoC accepted. tagging for staging run next Wed. :white_check_mark:

emma: i'll draft manifest schema PR tonight. ping here when ready. :rocket:
